source_scope.ag_thermodynamics: The user-provided summary attributes Ag heat capacity, melting point, latent heat, and density anchors to NIST/CDC thermophysical tables.
source_scope.ag_thermal_conductivity: The user-provided summary attributes solid and liquid conductivity anchors to NIST recommended data; the liquid value is described there as tentative.
source_scope.ti3sic2: Barsoum et al. (1999), Sections 3.3–3.4, provide empirical correlations for Cp and total thermal conductivity. Barsoum report DSC Cp measurements from 100–1000 C and extrapolate Cp to about 1200 C; the thermal-conductivity fit covers 25–1200 C with R^2=0.86. Qiu et al. (2020), Section 2.3, repeats these correlations and states 25–1600 C for Cp, but this is a secondary review of the same underlying experimental work, not an independent high-temperature dataset. Togo et al. (2010) provide first-principles Cp through 1400 K; Wang and Zhou (2004) provide first-principles Cv at 300, 700, 1100 and 1500 K; Son et al. (2016) provide calculated Cp through 1000 K. These are cross-checks, not 2000 K validation.
source_scope.provenance_limit: The user-provided PDFs for Barsoum et al. (1999), Togo et al. (2010), Wang and Zhou (2004), Son et al. (2016), and Qiu et al. (2020) were reviewed. The repository records the selected correlations and checkpoint values, but does not store digitized raw figure data or full uncertainty arrays. Ag source-table provenance remains incomplete.

ag.thermal_density_policy: Use fixed solid reference density for the first enthalpy-volume solver; do not claim thermal expansion or liquid-volume change is modeled.
ag.solid_cp_interpolation: Piecewise linear in temperature through thermophysical_candidates.csv anchors at 300 K and Tm.
ag.liquid_cp_interpolation: Constant at the single supplied melting-point anchor; no temperature trend is inferred.
ag.solid_conductivity_interpolation: Piecewise linear between 300 K and Tm anchors.
ag.liquid_conductivity_interpolation: Constant at the single supplied melting-point anchor; tentative source status remains attached.

ti3sic2.density_policy: Fixed reference density retained from the existing project configuration; thermal expansion is not coupled into density or volumetric enthalpy.

cp_model.source: Barsoum et al. (1999), Section 3.3, Fig. 5; correlation repeated in Qiu et al. (2020), Eq. (25)
cp_model.extension_status: 2000 K is an extrapolation beyond the primary paper's reported Cp range and beyond the range stated by the secondary review.

conductivity_model.source: Barsoum et al. (1999), Section 3.4, Fig. 6; correlation repeated in Qiu et al. (2020), Eq. (24)
conductivity_model.extension_status: 1473.15–2000 K is extrapolated beyond the reported fit range.

enthalpy_model.note: Analytic integral of the Barsoum molar Cp correlation after conversion with the configured molar mass. Below 300 K, the implementation holds Cp at its 300 K value.

validation_scope.togo_2010: Calculated Cp curves and comparison with Barsoum experimental points through 1400 K (Fig. 5).
validation_scope.wang_zhou_2004: Calculated Cv values at 300, 700, 1100 and 1500 K; the paper reports 115.0 and 147.7 J/(mol K) for alpha-Ti3SiC2 at 300 and 1500 K, respectively, compared with 110 and 153 experimental values. Cv is not Cp.
validation_scope.son_2016: Calculated Cp curve through 1000 K (Fig. 9); authors note a slight overestimate of experimental Cp above 300 K.
validation_scope.limit: No cited paper provides direct Ti3SiC2 Cp or k measurements at 2000 K.

source.note: The conversion uses 1 eV = 1.602176634e-19 J, 1 ps = 1e-12 s, and 1 Angstrom = 1e-10 m. Source power remains weighted by Ag volume fraction and is not renormalized after masking.

boundary_cases.A: Adiabatic scaffold: no heat flux through the Ag/skeleton boundary; pure geometric confinement baseline.
boundary_cases.B: Ideal thermal contact: shared temperature and continuous heat flux with a dynamically conducting and heat-storing Ti3SiC2 phase; zero added interface resistance.

extrapolation_policy: Single-temperature enthalpy solver only. Ti3SiC2 Cp uses the Barsoum et al. empirical relation Cp_molar=164.4-16419/T (T in K), analytically integrated for enthalpy. Ti3SiC2 k uses the Barsoum et al. linear fit k=38.6-0.0045*T. The 2000 K upper limit is a numerical/property-model guard, not a validated material-stability limit. Cp and especially k above their reported source ranges are extrapolations. Density remains fixed at 4520 kg/m^3.
